questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: Distributing free space with space-between
questions.stem: A lab flex row has four items with space-between; how many gaps between items?

options.text: No gaps because items touch.
Four gaps including outer edges.
Five gaps because space-between adds extras.
Three gaps between the four items.

questions.explanation: space-between creates n-1 gaps between n items. Including outer edges confuses with space-around.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: Counting the elements a descendant selector reaches
questions.stem: A lab rule uses div *; how many elements does it reach?

options.text: Only direct children of div.
Only the first descendant.
All descendant elements inside a div.
None because universal selector is invalid.

questions.explanation: div * matches all descendants at any depth. Child-only or first-only assumptions undercount.

questions.topic: Choosing the winning declaration among three rules
questions.stem: A lab shorthand declaration with !important conflicts with a longhand; which wins?

options.text: The longhand wins because it is more specific.
The browser picks randomly.
They merge into a combined shorthand.
The !important shorthand wins.

questions.explanation: !important on the shorthand overrides the conflicting longhand. Specificity or merging assumptions misapply cascade.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: Counting list items when an end tag is missing
questions.stem: A lab markup places a p inside an li without closing p; what happens?

options.text: The document is rejected as invalid.
The p closes immediately and content leaks.
The p closes when the li closes.
The p replaces the li.

questions.explanation: The p stays open until the li closes. Premature closure or rejection misreads parsing.
questions.hint: p closes with its parent li.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: Margins that stop collapsing inside a flex container
questions.stem: A lab has a block inside a flex item with vertical margins; do those margins collapse with the flex item's margins?

answer.exemplar: The nested block's margins can collapse with the flex item's margins only if no border or padding separates them, because collapse rules still apply within the item.

questions.explanation: Margin collapse can occur inside a flex item between its children and itself if unseparated. Assuming flex always prevents collapse overstates the rule.
questions.hint: Collapse can happen inside a flex item.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.learningObjective: Compare display none and visibility hidden
questions.stem: A lab needs an element gone from layout entirely; which property?

options.text: visibility hidden, which keeps layout space.
z-index negative, which removes layout space.
opacity zero, which removes layout space.
display none, which removes layout space.

questions.explanation: display none removes the element from layout. visibility hidden keeps space, and opacity or z-index misread layout.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.stem: A lab grid has gap 20px and two 1fr columns in 120px; what is each column?

options.text: 40px because gap is doubled.
60px because gap is ignored.
50px because 120 minus 20 gap splits 100 evenly.
120px because each fr takes full width.

questions.explanation: Subtract gap then split, 50px each. Ignoring or doubling gap miscounts.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.stem: A lab flex item with long text uses overflow hidden; does it allow shrinking?

options.text: No, overflow hidden does not change min-width auto.
No, because overflow hidden deletes content.
Yes, but only in Firefox.
Yes, overflow hidden automatically sets min-width 0.

questions.explanation: overflow hidden (or scroll/auto) makes min-width auto resolve to 0, allowing shrinking. Denying the effect misreads the spec.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.stem: A lab element declares width 100px with border-box; what is the rendered width?

options.text: 80px because extras are subtracted twice.
120px because extras add outside.
100px because border-box includes extras.
0px because border-box invalidates width.

questions.explanation: Border-box makes declared width include extras, so rendered width equals 100px. Content-box assumptions overstate it.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.stem: A lab technician asks which step fills in colors and text; what is it?

answer.exemplar: The paint step fills in pixels for text, colors, borders, and images based on the computed layout, before compositing layers.

questions.explanation: Paint fills visual pixels after layout. Layout only computes geometry, so confusing them misattributes rendering.
